stem: Each option below contains a group of three letters. Four groups share a common structural pattern. Which group does NOT follow the same pattern as the other three? (A) AEI (B) BDF (C) GKO (D) HIJ

per_option_rationale.rationale: AEI: positions 1, 5, 9 - a uniform skip of 4 between consecutive letters. It fits the equal-gap pattern. A student might flag it as the odd one because all three are vowels, but the structural property tested is alphabetical gap, not vowel status.
BDF: positions 2, 4, 6 - a uniform skip of 2. It fits the equal-gap pattern with a gap of 2.
GKO: positions 7, 11, 15 - a uniform skip of 4. It fits the equal-gap pattern. A student might flag GKO because the gap (4) is same as AEI while BDF has gap 2, but all three have equal gaps >=2.
HIJ: positions 8, 9, 10 - these are consecutive letters with a gap of only 1. AEI (gap 4), BDF (gap 2), and GKO (gap 4) all skip at least one letter between each pair; HIJ does not skip any letters.

explanation: The shared pattern in AEI, BDF, and GKO is a uniform inter-letter gap of 2 or more alphabetical positions (AEI: +4, +4; BDF: +2, +2; GKO: +4, +4). HIJ uses consecutive letters (H=8, I=9, J=10, gap=+1,+1) and breaks this pattern.

explanation_sections.punchline: The key structural property is the inter-letter gap size: the three correct groups skip letters, while HIJ does not.
explanation_sections.approach: Deductive trace: convert each letter to its alphabetical position and compute the gaps within each triplet. AEI: 1->5->9 (gap 4); BDF: 2->4->6 (gap 2); GKO: 7->11->15 (gap 4); HIJ: 8->9->10 (gap 1). Setup decision: identify inter-letter gap as the structural property to test.
explanation_sections.lesson: For letter-group odd-one-out, always compute the alphabetical position gaps within each group - consistent skipping is the most common structural pattern.
explanation_sections.timing: 60-70 seconds. Trap: focusing on vowel vs consonant status (AEI are all vowels) instead of the positional gap structure.
